title: Define gradual pinning and runtime compatibility clauses for open models
creator: Nina Patel
description: Clarify product requirements for onboarding new open-source model variants into the Redwood model catalog. The goal is to define a gradual pinning model (soft -> hard), runtime compatibility clauses that determine when a variant can be served without manual intervention, and explicit compatibility notes that appear in the catalog UI and API responses. This ticket consolidates prior intake discussions and proposes acceptance criteria, rollout phases, and guardrails for both hosted and Dedicated/Private deployments.
scope_changes: Initial intake asked only for a binary pinned/unpinned flag — expanded to include a 3-state pinning: 'soft-pin', 'locked-pin', 'unpinned'
Compatibility metadata extended to include kernel affinity, sequence-length profile, and quantization-safety tag
Added explicit requirement for catalog UI to show 'compatibility confidence' score and automated fallback mapping
decisions: Adopt 3-state pinning: soft-pin (recommended runtime), locked-pin (serve only pinned runtime), unpinned (runtime chooses best-fit variant)

Compatibility signal set will be a combination of a boolean compatibility_pass and a short list of 'incompatibility reasons' strings (e.g., 'KV_CACHE_MISMATCH', 'QUANT_BLOCKED', 'ATTENTION_KERNEL_MISMATCH')
Runtime will consult a lightweight compat manifest at request time and may fallback to a compatible variant if soft-pin fails under policy limits
Catalog API will expose 'compatibility_notes' (up to 3 strings) and a numeric 'compat_confidence' 0-100 for display and programmatic consumption
open_questions: How frequently should runtime re-evaluate soft-pin eligibility? (per-request, periodic, or event-driven)
Do we require a model author-signed compatibility statement for locked-pin? If so, what format and verification?
What is the SLA implication if a locked-pin model fails on Dedicated nodes during an upgrade?
Should the compatibility_confidence be surfaced in billing/optimizer decisions?
acceptance_criteria: Specification document describing 3-state pinning semantics, state transitions, and UX hints is reviewed and merged
API contract: catalog GET/POST exposes 'pin_state', 'compatibility_notes', 'compat_confidence' and matches sample OpenAPI fragment in the PRD
Runtime prototype honors soft-pin for at least the two common fallbacks (compatible-variant substitution and regional routing) with feature-flag gating
Console shows compatibility_notes and a tooltip with reasons, and PM/Support can filter catalog by pin_state and compat_confidence
Security team sign-off if security_review_required=true; any locked-pin policy must include a verification checklist
